title: Disney agrees to hire the majority of Character.AI’s workforce
slides: Why is Disney hiring Character.AI's entire team?
Character.AI built chatbots users talk to for hours
Disney wants that engagement inside its own IP
Your next Disney character may remember past chats
Watch which characters get memory first
thread_text:
1. Disney's AI talent grab

Disney hired the entire Character.AI team. That's not an acquisition—it's a direct signal that the House of Mouse wants conversational AI under its roof.

2. Users talk for hours

Character.AI's chatbots keep people engaged for hours. That level of stickiness is exactly what Disney wants for its own characters.

3. Engagement meets IP

Disney plans to fold that engagement into its own intellectual property. Imagine talking to a Disney character that feels as responsive as a Character.AI bot.

4. Memory changes everything

Your next Disney character may remember past chats. That means continuity across visits—and a much deeper emotional connection.

5. Which characters first?

Take a guess: which Disney character would you want to have memory? Reply with your pick—and watch which ones get it first.

instagram.caption:
Your next Disney character might remember your last conversation. Disney agreed to hire the majority of Character.AI's workforce — not buy the company, just take the team.

Character.AI built chatbots people talk to for hours, and that stickiness is what Disney wants inside its own characters.

Folding that engagement into Disney's intellectual property means continuity across visits, not fresh small talk every time.

If you write or build with characters, memory becomes the feature to watch — a character that recalls past chats changes how stories get written.

Which Disney character would you want to have memory first? 👀🕰️💬
